title: Chapter 10: The Investor and His Advisers; Zweig commentary

claims.text: Advice can earn its cost by preventing mistakes and supporting a suitable plan; paying for advice does not establish a right to excess returns or prove the adviser can deliver them.
Evaluate recommendations in relation to current price and long-term earning power, rather than treating favorable near-term business prospects as a sufficient purchase signal.

Identify the compensation and commercial role behind advice. Commission incentives and an underwriter's seller role can conflict with the purchaser's interests even when the intermediary is reputable.
Retain responsibility for understanding the recommendation, its evidence and its fit to the mandate; outside suggestions are inputs to judgment rather than automatic trade authority.
Verify professional records independently and continue monitoring after selection. A referral, credential or comfortable conversation is not a substitute for the underlying disclosure record.
claims.anchor: independently obtain your own complete copy

claims.text: An explicit mutually agreed investment policy, allocation and financial plan can make advice auditable and reduce impulsive departures; reporting must let the client understand progress and actual dollar fees.

assimilation: For this Character, advice must retain provenance, incentive context and a stated reason for agreement or disagreement. Initial independent judgment precedes bounded advice; an adviser cannot expand the mandate. Explain expected service value, costs and review triggers without promising superior returns. Preserve owner authority through a readable policy and reports.
adversarial_review: The source's praise of brokerage ethics and institutional competence is not diligence evidence. Its banking custody procedure, registrations, fee ceiling and expected-return range are historical and require current verification before operational use. Warning phrases are prompts for scrutiny, not a fraud classifier: options, commodities or monthly reporting are not intrinsically fraudulent. An automatic refusal of every timing approach or every sale after a weak year would replace analysis with a label. The proper question is whether the rule was supported, preregistered and within risk limits. References can be selected; credentials do not prove integrity. No external adviser is hired and no order authority is granted by assimilating this chapter.
memory_delta: Require intelligible advice, independent evidence, incentive disclosure and mandate fit. Value error prevention separately from alpha. Keep initial opinions independent and record whether later advice changes them and why.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 241-262, including both adviser/client interview lists and the warning-phrase sidebar. This chapter contains no numerical figure requiring image extraction.
